Discusses copy-on-write memory management, not pipe EOF.

grades.quote: The pipe code sleeps inside a loop checking the sleep condition; if there are multiple readers or writers, all but the first process to wake up will see the condition is false and sleep again.
grades.reason: Provides background on pipe blocking and wakeups, but does not explain EOF or open write-end descriptors.

grades.quote: If no data is available, a read on a pipe waits for either data to be written or for all file descriptors referring to the write end to be closed; in the latter case, read will return 0, just as if the end of a data file had been reached.
grades.reason: Directly explains that EOF requires all write-end descriptors to close; a child's exit alone is insufficient if another write-end descriptor remains open.
